item.title: Gov’t, GBPA urged: Release $357m dispute verdict quick
item.description: The outcome of the $357m Grand Bahama Port Authority (GBPA) arbitration dispute must be swiftly disclosed to uphold business and investor confidence, it was argued yesterday, amid subtle hints the verdict may not have gone fully the Government’s way.

item.title: PM declines to give details of ‘partial’ ruling in $357m GBPA arbitration
item.description: PRIME Minister Philip “Brave” Davis said yesterday that an arbitration panel has issued a “partial” decision in the government’s high-stakes dispute with the Grand Bahama Port Authority but declined to disclose its substance, citing confidentiality.

item.title: Davis declines comment on active officer in $10k bribery allegation
item.description: PRIME Minister Philip “Brave” Davis declined yesterday to comment on reports that a high-ranking police officer remains on active duty after allegedly receiving $10,000 in a Supreme Court bribery case involving voice notes and a $1.475m airport bank security heist.

item.title: PM says rent control bill unlikely to reach parliament before upcoming general election
item.description: RENT control legislation is unlikely to reach Parliament before the next general election, Prime Minister Philip “Brave” Davis said yesterday, signalling that one of the government’s most closely watched housing pledges may slip beyond its current term.

item.title: Commission launches three years after Protection Against Violence Act gazetted
item.description: THE government has formally appointed the Protection Against Violence Commission, activating a key enforcement body under the Protection Against Violence Act, 2023, nearly three years after the law was gazetted.

item.title: Man remanded to prison for Harbour Island double murder
item.description: A 26-year-old man accused of gunning down two men outside a Harbour Island bar last month was remanded to prison yesterday.

item.title: Four Bahamian scientists represent nation at global ocean conference
item.description: FOUR Bahamian scientists are representing the country at one of the world’s largest ocean research gatherings, the Ocean Sciences Meeting in Glasgow, Scotland.

item.title: Bahamian authors at heart of literacy push
item.description: BOOKS written by Bahamians were placed directly into the hands of young readers this week as part of a national literacy initiative tied to the country’s 52nd Independence celebrations.

item.title: Govt’s $357m claim against GBPA dismissed in full
item.description: The Government’s $357 million reimbursement claim against the Grand Bahama Port Authority (GBPA) has been dismissed in full by an Arbitration Tribunal in what the GBPA is describing as a landmark ruling for Freeport and Grand Bahama.

item.title: AG calls Tribunal ruling "monumental win", pushes back on GBPA statement
item.description: Attorney General Ryan Pinder today accused the Grand Bahama Port Authority of mischaracterising the arbitration ruling between the two parties, revealing that the GBPA failed in its bid seeking “over a $1 billion” in damages against the Government.
